# False-positive review log

Reviewed failures, newest last. Format: references/false-positive-review.md ("Record").

## iter-1 (e4947374c51cfdaaffd0d6ff6ae5dc10-63-12, live, 6.0-alpha2, network faults only) · audited bank balances sum to the initial total · real (adversarial check pending)
- Evidence: client `bank_autoretry` audits, 8 of ~302 (all failures come from `bank_autoretry`. No `bank_audit`, `bank_audit_final` or `bank_transfers` audit failed, but `bank_transfers` produced only 29 audits). Moment 3115707109627864019 @ 238.69260995578952: total 11992 (a0=1222, a1=1162, b100=608, other accounts 1000). The same state is read again @ 238.8134581767954 by a *different* client process through a different coordinator (10.89.0.2, then 10.89.0.4), so the bad state is stored, not a one-off bad read. Moment 2977298595378160927 @ 249.78711780183949: total 11938. a1 shows -62 with xfers=1, but the matching +62 credit to accounts_b:105 is missing (b105=1000, xfers=0) even though this client saw that transfer acknowledged (floor 1). By 252.09 (hash -9036390600776264542) b105=1062 is visible and the total is 12144: the late credit arrived, and a 144 debit on b100 was lost. Faults: only network partition, slow and clog faults. Gossip DOWN/UP and ReconfigureAccordFastPath epoch changes appear, with large ACCORD_* message drops. Node1 logs an NPE @ 235.33 in the read-txn failure path (`ExecuteTxn.onDone` calls `persist(... result=null)`, which hits `TxnAdapter.persist` → `result.toPersistable()`, CoordinationAdapter.java:296). That is a separate, minor SUT bug. Logs: scratchbook/logs/iter1-3115707109627864019.log, iter1-2977298595378160927.log. Log link: not available yet (`log_url.py --run` found no session_id while the run is in progress). Rerun it after the run completes.
- Checklist hit: clean.
  1. Every transfer is one `BEGIN TRANSACTION`. It computes new values inside the transaction (`SET balance -= a, xfers += 1` on both rows under `IF src.balance >= a`; helper_accord.py `transfer_cql`), never from a value the client read earlier. A resubmitted or driver-retried transfer is a new, money-conserving transaction, so "applied once or more" cannot change the total.
  2. The audit is one read-only transaction with 12 LETs over both tables, at default_fetch_size 1000 (one page, never split).
  3. Tables are created fresh `WITH transactional_mode='full'`, so migration_from is `none`. `TransactionalMode.readCLForMode` returns null, so the transaction takes the plain Accord path, not interop. onboarding-to-accord.adoc says that in `full`, all reads and writes execute on Accord.
  4. The seed is one conditional transaction that completes before `setup_complete` (log 205.2448 → 205.2475).
  5. No other command writes `accounts` or `accounts_b`.
  6. No orchestration, no clock faults, no node kills.
  Possible lines of defence for the adversarial reviewer: `accord.recover_txn: 1s*attempts<=10s` (production default 5s*attempts<=60s) makes recovery race live coordinators more often. That only changes timing and does not relax any safety setting. The record is also thin: autoretry does not log each attempt's error, so the transfer history cannot be fully rebuilt.
- Fix: none (not harness-caused). To strengthen the evidence: log every autoretry attempt (outcome, error type, coordinator) and every acknowledged transfer's reads, and log each audit snapshot to stdout, so the triage digest can rebuild the history.
- Re-run: —

## iter-1 (e4947374c51cfdaaffd0d6ff6ae5dc10-63-12) · audited transfer counters sum to an even number · real (adversarial check pending)
- Evidence: same moments. 3115707109627864019 @ 238.69: xfers a0=5, a1=5, b100=5, sum 15. 2977298595378160927 @ 249.787: sum 5. Later sums 9, 11, 11. Each transfer adds +1 to both of its accounts in one transaction. So for any set of whole transfers, each applied any number of times, the sum is even, whatever the client did (retries, ambiguity, resubmits). An odd sum read by one audit transaction can only come from a non-atomic apply, a lost update (one transaction reads stale data for a key, then overwrites a committed write: the b100 sequence in 2977… fits this), or a non-snapshot audit read. All three violate the documented guarantee.
- Checklist hit: clean (same analysis as above).
- Fix: none.
- Re-run: —

## iter-1 (e4947374c51cfdaaffd0d6ff6ae5dc10-63-12) · an audit reflects every transfer acknowledged or observed before it started · real (adversarial check pending)
- Evidence: 2977298595378160927 @ 249.78715482284315 (also on branch 937079777835102458 @ 249.815). regressions={accounts_b:105: floor 1, seen 0}. This client got an ack for a transfer that wrote b105.xfers=1 (it read 0 and the IF held), but its next audit sees b105 xfers=0, balance=1000. The credit shows up later (252.09). Floors are per process, are raised only from acknowledged reads or completed audits, and are never raised by ambiguous attempts. An audit starts strictly after the ack, so this is a strict-serializability (real-time) violation: a stale read.
- Checklist hit: clean (1: ambiguous outcomes never raise floors; 5: no state shared between processes).
- Fix: none.
- Re-run: —

## iterate-3 (126cbacda11c1e49afda49c425a00f31-63-12, full faults) + fix-verify-acked-transfer-overwritten-2 (0e1949506e0ec5407eb17348c627c8a3-63-12) · container: cassandra-accord-node2/node3, exit code: 3 · false-positive
- Evidence: node3 @ 142.05 (A, hash -3183840148574514038): `ERROR CassandraDaemon.java:1023 - Exception encountered during startup: The seed provider lists no seeds.` (ConfigurationException, DatabaseDescriptor.java:1661). node3 was restarting after node/stop at 138.84, and node1 was killed at 141.21. The only seed, `cassandra-accord-node1`, does not resolve while node1's container is down, so SimpleSeedProvider skips it and the list is empty. 142.37 exit=3, and the node never comes back in that history. Run-wide events: every exit-3 has this message (A 8+8, B 6+4, exact match). Harness code never exits 3. Log: scratchbook/logs/iter3-m3183840148574514038.log, link: https://honey-whale.antithesis.com/search?
- Checklist hit: 3 (configuration/topology: a single seed, so a restarting node depends on another container being up).
- Fix: render a non-empty seed list on restart. sut/cassandra-overrides.yaml: `- seeds: "__SEEDS__"`. sut/entrypoint.sh, before the sed: `if [[ -d /var/lib/cassandra/data/system ]]; then SEEDS="cassandra-accord-node1,cassandra-accord-node2,cassandra-accord-node3"; else SEEDS="cassandra-accord-node1"; fi` and `sed -e "s/__HOSTNAME__/${HOST}/g" -e "s/__SEEDS__/${SEEDS}/g" …`. First boot is unchanged (node1 is the only seed, so FIRST_CMS/VOTE behaves as before). On restart the node's own name always resolves (hasAnyEpoch=true, so NORMAL mode, which only needs a non-empty list). With static IPs (next entry) the IP literals can be used as seeds instead.
- Re-run: fixed in harness (sut/entrypoint.sh + cassandra-overrides.yaml); local kill test passed (logs/local-restart-test.txt); awaiting next Antithesis run.

## iterate-3 + fix-verify-acked-transfer-overwritten-2 · Guarantee 5 "a transaction / every node coordinated / a plain write and read … within 120 seconds after faults stopped" · false-positive
- Evidence: A (hash -9161517995650739017 @ 263.71): node2 and node3 killed at 141.0/143.5 and restarted with **new IPs** 10.89.0.6/10.89.0.7 (previously .3/.4). node1 logs `Could not find Node.Id for endpoint /10.89.0.6:7000`. All nodes keep dialling the stale .3/.4. 167.03 node1 `Caught an exception while trying to CAS: UnavailableException: Cannot achieve consistency level SERIAL 2 > 1`: the 3-member CMS has 2 members at stale addresses, so the restarted nodes' `Startup` (address-change) transformation can never commit. Recovery probe: 34 attempts over 119 s, WriteTimeout via node1, "10.89.0.6/.7 not in driver metadata". B (hash -7563627453930811647 @ 274.11): node1 (→.6) and node2 (→.7) restarted about 13 s apart. node1 committed STARTUP only after its catch-up timed out (158.8), by which time node2 had been re-addressed too, so node3 hit the same CAS Unavailable. Antithesis docs (fault_types, Node termination): "Restarted nodes may change IP addresses upon rejoining the network". Log: scratchbook/logs/iter3-m9161517995650739017.log, link: https://honey-whale.antithesis.com/search?; scratchbook/logs/fv2-m7563627453930811647.log, link: https://honey-whale.antithesis.com/search?
- Checklist hit: 3 (topology/environment: container restarts re-address a majority of the CMS, which production nodes with stable addresses don't do). Possible SUT lead (not a violation): TCM cannot recover when most CMS members change address before the change commits. Mention it in the method notes.
- Fix: give the nodes static addresses. config/docker-compose.yaml (and the config-fixverify-* copies): top-level `networks: {accord: {ipam: {config: [{subnet: 10.89.100.0/24}]}}}`, and per service `networks: {accord: {ipv4_address: 10.89.100.11}}` (node1), .12 (node2), .13 (node3), .20 (client). Run `snouty validate`. If Antithesis does not honour `ipv4_address` across restarts, record a harness-gap (IP churn) and report Guarantee 5 under "unconfirmed: possible harness involvement".
- Re-run: fixed in harness (config/docker-compose.yaml network accord 10.231.17.0/24, static ipv4_address; config-fixverify-* copies not re-rendered); local restart kept IPs; Antithesis docs do not document ipv4_address persistence, so verify in the next run.

## fix-verify-acked-transfer-overwritten-2 · audited bank balances sum to the initial total / audited transfer counters sum to an even number · suspect
- Evidence: hash 1866202673575119510 @ 200.680. The bank_transfers audit (client pid 132) via coordinator **10.89.0.6 = node2**: total 11939, xfer sum 155 (odd). node2 had a graceful stop (shutdown hook 155.60, `Cassandra shutdown complete` 159.93, node/stop fault logged 160.33, exit 143 at 160.62, safe-stop marker written, no stop-marker warning at restart), then restarted with a new IP (.3 → .6). 188.88 `ERROR AccordService.java:764 - Could not catchup with peers; continuing to startup`, STARTUP committed, `Startup complete` at 194.41. node1 killed at 199.62 and still down at the audit. All earlier audits in this history passed (last 181.73 via node3). Log: scratchbook/logs/fv2-1866202673575119510.log (+ .ndjson), link: https://honey-whale.antithesis.com/search?
- Checklist hit: 3 (an environment factor sits immediately before the symptom: the coordinator re-joined under a new IP after a failed catch-up). ALLOW_UNSAFE_STARTUP was **not** exercised (graceful stop, and node1 had not restarted yet). Items 1, 2, 4 and 5 are clean, as in the iterate-1 Guarantee 1 entries. Note for future restart failures: AccordTask replies only after `saveCommand(…, onFlush)` → `segments.onDurable` (PERIODIC: after the covering fsync), so acknowledged votes are fsynced. But the Antithesis docs do not promise that unsynced page cache survives a restart, and the stop marker also covers data applied via the periodic (10 s) commitlog and store state. A failure after an ALLOW_UNSAFE_STARTUP restart would therefore be `undetermined` at best.
- Fix: harness: the static-IP fix above removes the IP-change confound. Tighten: add `Reachable("an audit was coordinated by a node within 30 s of its restart")` and log the coordinator's restart time in the audit details. If it recurs with stable addresses, send it to the adversarial reviewer as a candidate new bug: "a node that continued startup after a failed Accord catch-up served a non-serializable read".
- Re-run: tightened: check_audit details now carry coordinator_node (hostname resolved from the coordinator address) next to coordinator; no restart inference added.

## hunt-3 (c16f5775) · default "container: cassandra-accord-node2, exit code: 3" (45) · real (SUT bug candidate), recorded here so later hunts don't re-triage it
- Evidence: hash -8545236388639200513 @ 224.71. First `JournalReadError in /var/lib/cassandra/accord_journal/log-1791488061546-1-1-1.data` at 224.19, after `node/kill node2` at 217.58. All 39 matching events are this one segment on node2. Stack: `EntrySerializer.validateCRC:259 ← tryRead:144 ← StaticSegment$SequentialReader.doAdvance:439/462 ← Metadata.rebuild:142 ← StaticSegment.open:121 ← Journal.open:219 ← AccordJournal.open:126 ← AccordService.localStartup:573`. Log: scratchbook/logs/hunt3--8545236388639200513.log. Link: https://honey-whale.antithesis.com/search?
- Checklist: clean. (1) The harness entrypoint, seeds and commitlog replay all succeed. (2) The process kill keeps the page cache, so this is the gentlest crash model. (3) ALLOW_UNSAFE_STARTUP only gets the run past the stop-marker gate, and REBOOTSTRAP would hit the same `journal.open`. The default `crc_failure_on_rebuild_policy=FAIL` together with rebuild's `fsyncedLimit=Integer.MAX_VALUE` turns a torn tail record (size marker set, CRC 0) into a fatal error. hunt-1 node3 exit 3 (37) and hunt-2 node3/node2 startup exceptions are probably the same failure (not verified).
- Fix: none applied (frozen). Candidate SUT fix: in `Metadata.rebuild`/`SequentialReader` treat a CRC-0 record (allocated, never written) in the last segment of a crashed process as end of segment, or make `IGNORE_CRC_ZERO_RECORDS` the default for rebuild.
